author: Old Dominion News
title: Dustin Groves named finalist for 2026 Jan Strickland Award
text:
Virginia men’s golf associate head coach Dustin Groves was named on Apr. 15 as one of five Division I finalists for the 2026 Jan Strickland Award presented by TaylorMade Golf Company. The award is given each year to an assistant coach who has excelled in supporting student-athletes both academically and athletically.
The recognition highlights Groves’s impact on the Virginia men’s golf program, which has achieved high national rankings throughout the season. Under his guidance, the team has recorded eight top two finishes and five victories, winning by an average margin of more than 11 strokes. Four Cavaliers players are ranked inside the top 50 nationally, led by Ben James, who is ranked second and is noted as the first three-time PING First Team All-American in program history.
Groves joined Virginia as an assistant coach in August 2022 after being hired by Bowen Sargent, who won the Jan Strickland Award in 2004. He was promoted to associate head coach at the end of the 2024-25 season. The Cavaliers are also noted as being the only men’s Division I program to reach NCAA Championship Match Play each of the last three seasons and secured their first Atlantic Coast Conference championship in 2025.
Other Division I finalists for this year’s award include Noah Goldman from North Carolina, Jace Long from Louisiana State University (LSU), Gustavo Morantes from Arkansas, and James Vargas from Texas Tech. Finalists were also named from NCAA Division II and NJCAA Division II programs.
Two assistant coaches—one from a Division I school and one from a non-Division I institution—will be selected as recipients of the Jan Strickland Outstanding Assistant Coach Award presented by TaylorMade Golf Company.
